$comment: SecurityInsight field catalog. Every SI field is defined once here. Template kind: field-catalog. Customer overrides go in field-catalog.custom.json (per field, by name).

levels.both: on the record, and resolved onto the CI

policies.authority: fresh candidates only (record age <= staleDays); the first provider in the authority list wins; no fresh candidate -> the newest value, marked stale
policies.any_true: true when any fresh candidate is true
policies.union: the union of every fresh candidate (lists), de-duplicated
policies.min: the smallest value of any candidate
policies.max: the largest value of any candidate
policies.computed: set by SecurityInsight (correlation, enrichment or analysis), never mapped from a provider

authorityTokens.cmdb_owner: the tenant's ONE CMDB owner: cmdb (SecurityInsight's own) or servicenow

origins.synced: an identity synchronised from Active Directory: an Active Directory record is linked to the CI, or a provider says onPremisesSyncEnabled
origins.cloud: a cloud-only identity: an Entra record is linked and nothing says it is synchronised
origins.byOrigin: resolution.byOrigin.<origin> = { policy, authority, decidedBy }: for that origin ONLY the authority providers may supply the value; decidedBy (default: authority) = one of them must be linked for the value, or its absence, to be known. Otherwise -- or when the origin cannot be told -- the field is in si_unknown_fields and no risk factor raises on it. Customer-overridable per field (field-catalog.custom.json / Pro cfg.ItemOverride 'field-catalog:<field>').

fields.name: si_record_key

fields.name: si_provider
fields.description: The provider that reported the record (mde, entra, azure, eg, mdi, intune, ad, shodan, cmdb, servicenow).

fields.name: si_record_type

fields.name: si_first_seen

fields.name: si_last_seen

fields.name: si_record_state

fields.name: si_lifecycle

fields.name: si_lifecycle_reason

fields.name: si_not_seen_days
fields.description: A not seen or retired CI: whole days since any source last saw it (empty while active).

fields.name: si_linked_objects

fields.name: si_ci_action
fields.description: What the ledger did for the CI this run: mint (new), reuse or merge.

fields.name: si_link_count
fields.description: Number of linked records.

fields.name: si_owner_ci_id

finding.description: On a finding: the business services of the asset it is on (the CI's si_services).

fields.description: The keys of the business services this CI belongs to, sorted.

fields.name: si_service_count
fields.description: How many business services this CI belongs to. 0 = an unowned CI.

fields.name: si_service_orphan
fields.description: True when no business service owns this CI (it is listed among the unowned CIs).

fields.name: si_service_owner
fields.description: The owner inherited from the business services: the owner of the most critical service the CI belongs to.

fields.name: si_service_criticality
fields.description: The business criticality inherited from the services: the strictest of them (by the criticality mapping's factor).

fields.name: si_service_criticality_level
fields.description: The inherited criticality as a level: critical, high, medium or low.

fields.name: si_service_data_sensitivity

fields.name: si_service_environment

fields.name: si_service_department
fields.description: The owning department of the most critical service the CI belongs to.

fields.name: si_is_break_glass
fields.description: Emergency-access (break-glass) account -- a CLASSIFICATION, not a risk factor: the identity profiler's value on the Entra record, OR the platform signals and naming patterns of the data-model list break_glass_patterns (an emergency-access group, a break-glass name; the customer overrides the list), OR the extension attribute and value the customer defines (list break_glass_attribute, si_break_glass_attribute), OR exclusion from ALL the enabled Conditional Access policies that would apply to the account (si_ca_excluded_from_all -- one excluding policy is not enough). si_break_glass_reason says which rule matched. Feeds the tier rules and the break-glass reports.

fields.name: si_onprem_synced
fields.description: Synchronised from on-premises AD.

fields.name: si_created
fields.description: Creation time.

fields.name: si_last_sign_in
fields.description: Last successful sign-in (interactive or non-interactive). A synchronised account signs in on-premises too: the newest of Active Directory (lastLogonTimestamp), Defender for Identity and Entra, KNOWN only when its Active Directory record is linked (the Defender for Identity record SecurityInsight captures -- the IdentityInfo row -- carries no sign-in, so it cannot decide one); a cloud-only account: Entra. Not known = unknown, never stale or never signed in.

fields.name: si_password_last_changed
fields.description: Last password change. A synchronised account changes its password in Active Directory (pwdLastSet) -- Entra's lastPasswordChangeDateTime follows it only with password hash sync -- so it takes Active Directory, then Defender for Identity / Exposure Graph on-premises data, never Entra; a cloud-only account takes Entra. Not decidable = unknown, never old.

fields.name: si_ca_excluded_policies
fields.description: The ENABLED Conditional Access policies that would apply to the user but EXCLUDE it -- directly, through a group or through a role: { id, name } each. A policy that never included the user is not listed. Context: being excluded from one policy is not break-glass (si_ca_excluded_from_all says whether EVERY policy that would apply excludes the user). Never holds anything but policies: a missing licence is said in si_not_licensed.

fields.name: si_ca_excluded_from_all
fields.description: Yes when at least one ENABLED Conditional Access policy would apply to the user and EVERY one of them excludes it (the policies are listed in si_ca_excluded_policies) -- one of the two break-glass rules. No when a policy applies to the user, or none would apply at all. Empty = it could not be told (a group a policy names could not be read, or the policies were not read).

fields.name: si_break_glass_attribute
fields.description: The extension attribute and value that mark the user as an emergency-access (break-glass) account, as attribute=value -- one of the entries YOU define in the data-model list break_glass_attribute (nothing is shipped). Empty = the user carries none of them, or no entry is defined.

fields.name: si_break_glass_reason
fields.description: WHY the account is classified break-glass, in one sentence naming every rule that matched: the identity collection marks it, a naming pattern (sign-in name, display name or a group's name), the extension attribute and value you defined, or exclusion from all the enabled Conditional Access policies that would apply to it. Empty when the account is not break-glass.

fields.name: si_passwordless_only
fields.description: The account signs in passwordless only: its sign-in methods (Microsoft Graph, permission UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All) were read in full, hold no password, and hold a way to sign in without one; the account is a cloud-only member account. A password that exists counts as usable. Unknown when the methods could not be read in full (permission not granted yet, Microsoft asked SecurityInsight to slow down, a partial read), and for a synchronised or guest account without a cloud password (its password lives elsewhere) -- a report reads unknown as 'may use a password', never as no.

fields.description: Defender for Identity investigation priority percentile, 0-100.

fields.name: si_manager_id
fields.description: The object id of the user's manager (Microsoft Graph, the manager relation). Shown next to the manager's sign-in name and display name.

fields.name: si_manager_name
fields.description: The display name of the user's manager (Microsoft Graph; Defender for Identity's value where Entra has none).

fields.name: si_sponsors
fields.description: A guest's sponsors: { id, upn, name, type } each. A guest's sponsors are also its owner (si_owner).

fields.name: si_last_interactive_sign_in
fields.description: The user's last INTERACTIVE sign-in (Microsoft Graph signInActivity.lastSignInDateTime). si_last_sign_in is the newest of every kind; an account used only by a token refresh has a recent si_last_sign_in and an old value here.

fields.name: si_last_non_interactive_sign_in
fields.description: The user's last NON-interactive sign-in (a client or token refresh acting for the user; Microsoft Graph signInActivity.lastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime).

fields.name: si_mfa_strength
fields.description: The strongest way the user can do MFA, from the methods registered: phishing-resistant (FIDO2 key, passkey, Windows Hello for Business, certificate), strong (Microsoft Authenticator, a one-time code), weak (phone call or text message), none. Empty = the registration was not read (unknown).

fields.name: si_mfa_default_method
fields.description: The user's default MFA method (Microsoft Graph userRegistrationDetails.defaultMfaMethod).

fields.name: si_ca_mfa_enforced
fields.description: Conditional Access enforces MFA for the user: an ENABLED policy that applies to the user (included, not excluded) requires MFA or an authentication strength for ALL cloud apps, with nothing else able to satisfy it instead. False = no such policy. Empty = unknown (the policies, or the members of a group one of them names, could not be read). Locations, device platforms and risk conditions are not evaluated; security defaults are not Conditional Access.

fields.name: si_ca_policy_count
fields.description: How many ENABLED Conditional Access policies apply to the user (included and not excluded).

fields.name: si_ca_mfa_policies
fields.description: The Conditional Access policies that enforce MFA for the user: { id, name } each.

fields.name: si_entra_risk_level
fields.description: Identity Protection risk level of the user or service principal: none, low, medium, high, hidden. Empty = not listed as risky; see si_not_licensed when the tenant has no licence for it.

fields.name: si_entra_risk_state
fields.description: Identity Protection risk state: atRisk, confirmedCompromised, remediated, dismissed, confirmedSafe.

fields.name: si_entra_risk_detail
fields.description: Identity Protection risk detail: why the risk state is what it is (for example adminConfirmedUserCompromised, userPerformedSecuredPasswordChange).

fields.name: si_entra_risk_updated
fields.description: When Identity Protection last updated the risk of the identity.

fields.name: si_risk_detections_30d
fields.description: Identity Protection risk detections for the user in the last 30 days (counted while the detections are read; the detections themselves are not stored).

fields.name: si_risk_detection_types_30d
fields.description: The kinds of Identity Protection risk detections for the user in the last 30 days (for example unfamiliarFeatures, leakedCredentials).

fields.name: si_entra_role_scopes
fields.description: Every Entra role assignment of the identity WITH its scope: { role, roleId, assignment (active, eligible, activated), scopeType (tenant, administrative unit, object), scopeId, scopeName, tenantWide, activatedUntil }. A role held through a group the identity is a member of only while an eligible membership is activated is listed too, as activated, with the group (via, viaGroupId) and until when the membership lasts (membershipActivatedUntil). A role scoped to an administrative unit or one object is not a tenant-wide role and does not decide the privilege tier.

fields.name: si_role_paths
fields.description: HOW the identity holds, or can get, each Entra role -- one line per path: "Global Administrator (direct)", "Group IT Admins -> User Administrator", "Group Tier0 (can activate) -> Global Administrator", "User Administrator (direct, administrative unit Sales)", "Global Administrator via Tier0 Admins (eligible, activated until 2026-10-11T18:00:00Z)" (a member of the group only while an eligible membership is activated).

fields.name: si_pim_activation_requires
fields.description: What activating each of the identity's eligible roles requires (Privileged Identity Management role settings): { role, roleId, requires (MFA, justification, ticket, approval, authentication context), maxDuration }. An eligible Tier 0 role that requires nothing is as good as permanent.

fields.name: si_controls_privileged_objects
fields.description: The privileged objects the identity OWNS: a group that holds an Entra role, a service principal that holds one, or that principal's application registration -- { kind, id, name, roles }. An owner can add a member or a credential and so take the role.

fields.name: si_last_access_review
fields.description: The last access review of what the identity holds: per reviewed role, group or application { kind, id, name, reviewId, reviewName, lastReviewed, status }. Empty = nothing it holds is under review.

fields.name: si_last_access_review_date
fields.description: The newest completed access review among the roles, groups and applications the identity holds.

fields.name: si_not_licensed
fields.description: The context this asset has no data for because the tenant is not licensed for it (for example Entra ID P2, Defender for Identity, Microsoft Intune): the fields that need the licence say "not licensed (<licence>)" -- empty because of the licence, never because there is no risk. Set ONLY when the source itself answers that the licence is missing; a source that is merely empty says "no data (licence missing or not collected yet)" in its own field and is not listed here.

fields.name: si_has_federated_credential
fields.description: The application registration has a federated credential (workload identity federation: GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, another identity provider) -- it can sign in without a secret or certificate. False = the federated credentials were read and it has none.

fields.name: si_federated_credentials
fields.description: The application registration's federated credentials: { id, name, issuer, subject, audiences } each -- who may sign in as the application.

fields.name: si_requested_vs_granted_perms
fields.description: The permissions the application registration asks for against those granted: { requested, granted, requestedNotGranted, grantedNotRequested }. Granted but not requested = a permission given outside the manifest.

fields.name: si_owners
fields.description: The owners of the service principal AND of its application registration: { id, upn, name, type, of (service principal, application, or both when the same person owns the two) } each.

fields.name: si_owner_upns
fields.description: The sign-in names of the owners of the service principal and its application registration.

fields.name: si_owner_ids
fields.description: The object ids of the owners of the service principal and its application registration.

fields.name: si_consent_type
fields.description: How the delegated permissions were consented: admin (for every user), user (individual users consented), or admin and user.

fields.name: si_consented_user_count
fields.description: How many users consented individually to the application's delegated permissions (counted while the grants are read).

fields.name: si_delegated_grants
fields.description: The delegated permissions per API: { resourceId, resourceName, consentType, permissions, userCount } each.

fields.name: si_last_app_sign_in
fields.description: The last time the application signed in AS ITSELF (client credentials: a secret, certificate or federated credential).

fields.name: si_last_delegated_sign_in
fields.description: The last time the application signed in FOR A USER (delegated).

fields.name: si_credentials
fields.description: Every secret and certificate of the service principal and its application registration: { keyId, type (secret, certificate), name, on, expires, daysLeft, state (expired, expiring, active), lastUsed, neverUsed, usedAfterExpiry }. Never a secret's value.

fields.name: si_credential_fix
fields.description: What to do about the expired or expiring credentials, in one text: which secret or certificate (name and key id), on the service principal or the application registration, when it expires and when it was last used.

fields.name: si_attached_resource
fields.description: The Azure resource a managed identity belongs to (its name): the virtual machine, app or automation account of a system-assigned identity, or the identity resource of a user-assigned one.

fields.name: si_managed_identity_kind
fields.description: system-assigned or user-assigned (managed identities only).

fields.name: si_publisher_domain
fields.description: The verified publisher domain of the application registration.

fields.name: si_app_notes
fields.description: The notes on the application registration (often who owns it and what it is for).

fields.name: si_mdi_tags
fields.description: The tags Defender for Identity puts on the account (for example Sensitive, Honeytoken).

fields.name: si_is_honeytoken
fields.description: The account is tagged Honeytoken in Defender for Identity: a decoy, any sign-in is an alert. Empty = not tagged.

fields.name: si_onprem_last_logon
fields.description: The last successful Active Directory logon Defender for Identity saw in the last 30 days.

fields.name: si_cleartext_ldap
fields.description: Cleartext LDAP binds by the account in the last 30 days (Defender for Identity): its password crossed the network unprotected.

fields.name: si_ntlm_logons
fields.description: Successful NTLM logons by the account in the last 30 days (Defender for Identity).

fields.name: si_primary_user
fields.description: The sign-in name of the device's registered owner in Entra ID (the person who registered or joined it).

fields.name: si_registered_owners
fields.description: The registered owners of the Entra device: { id, upn, name, type } each.

fields.name: si_ms_criticality_reason
fields.description: WHY Microsoft Exposure Management rates the asset critical: the names of the criticality rules that matched (for example Global Administrator, Domain Controller).

fields.name: si_asset_subtype
fields.description: The asset's kind within its type, ONE value: SQL Server, SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, PostgreSQL, Domain controller, ... General when no classification row matches. Set by the classification rows (classifications.locked.json); every role stays in si_device_roles.

fields.name: si_asset_type_source
fields.description: The asset type as the sources gave it (Defender device type, Entra identity type, the Azure type's last segment), before the classification rows refined si_asset_type.

fields.name: si_components
fields.description: The components the asset carries (the component classification): every value a classification row proves -- a SQL Server VM is OS and SQL. Other when none matches, never blank.

fields.name: si_classified_by
fields.description: Per classification dimension (asset_type, asset_subtype, component, ...): the classification rows that decided the value, or fallback.

fields.name: si_sql_iaas
fields.description: The VM is registered with the SQL IaaS extension: a microsoft.sqlvirtualmachine/sqlvirtualmachines resource names it (si_sql_vm_resource_id). Set by the classification step of the CI build.

fields.name: si_sql_vm_resource_id
fields.description: On a microsoft.sqlvirtualmachine/sqlvirtualmachines resource: the resource id of the VM it registers (properties.virtualMachineResourceId), lower case.

fields.name: si_component
fields.description: The component the finding concerns (the component classification): OS, SQL, Network, Hardware, Browser, Office, Application or Other -- ONE value, from the classification rows over the finding's own fields (an OS vulnerability on a SQL Server VM stays OS). Other when none matches, never blank. Carried to reports, exports and the ServiceNow vulnerable item (u_si_component) so the finding maps to the CI or its sub-CI.

fields.name: si_servicenow_subci
fields.description: ServiceNow sub-CI: the bucket ServiceNow links the finding under on its CI (shipped OS / SQL / Other: component OS -> OS, SQL -> SQL, everything else -> Other, the fallback bucket) -- ONE value, never blank, from the classification rows (the dimension servicenow_subci; the customer's rules on vendor, product, report, category or configuration id first, then the component). Configurable per install: Pro Settings > ServiceNow > Sub-CI mapping, Community dimensions.custom.json + classification.custom.json. Carried to reports, exports and the ServiceNow vulnerable item (u_si_servicenow_subci).

fields.name: si_subcategory
fields.description: The finding's subcategory as its source names it (Defender configuration ConfigurationSubcategory, Defender for Cloud security issue, the report's Subcategory).

fields.name: si_patch_cycle
fields.description: Patch cycle: ONE of In monthly cycle, Catch-up (older than 1 month), No fix available, Unknown -- never blank. In monthly cycle / Catch-up: the fix's release date (the month a 'October 2026 Security Updates' / '2026-10 Cumulative Update' text names -> that month's Patch Tuesday; an explicit date wins) or, without one dated update, the finding's first detection (SI's, else the source's first-seen si_source_first_seen), within / older than SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays (default 30) at the collection. No fix available when the source says none exists, or when the finding names no recommended update and nothing dates it (no single update); Unknown only for an update whose month cannot be read. From the classification rows patch-cycle-* (the customer may override them).

fields.name: si_patch_fix
fields.description: A fact the patch-cycle rows read: 'none' when the source says no fix exists for the finding.

fields.name: si_patch_age
fields.description: A fact the patch-cycle rows read: 'within' / 'over' -- the fix's release (else the finding's first detection) is within / older than SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays at the collection.

fields.name: si_affected_product
fields.description: The affected software product(s) of a vulnerability, as the source names them (Defender vulnerability management SoftwareName, e.g. sql_server_2019). Unknown when the source does not say.

fields.name: si_fix_release_date
fields.description: When the finding's fix was released: a Microsoft update's own release date by its KB, from Microsoft's public Security Update Guide (api.msrc.microsoft.com, read once a day and cached; Defender names the KB but not its date). Empty for a third-party fix. The patch cycle reads it first.

fields.name: si_cve_published
fields.description: When the CVE was published (Defender vulnerability management's PublishedDate, as si_published): the exposure age. The patch cycle does not read it -- a CVE's date is not its fix's.

fields.name: si_affected_vendor
fields.description: The affected software vendor(s) (Defender vulnerability management SoftwareVendor).

fields.name: si_affected_version
fields.description: The affected software version(s) (Defender vulnerability management SoftwareVersion).

fields.name: si_affected_cpe
fields.description: The affected product as a CPE (cpe:2.3:a:<vendor>:<product>:...), when a source gives one (Exposure Graph, Shodan).

fields.name: si_description
fields.description: WHAT: what the finding is and why it matters, as its source describes it (Defender vulnerability description, configuration / risk description, Defender for Cloud description, Exposure Graph description) or, for SI's own reports, the report's text (data-model/finding-texts.locked.json).

fields.name: si_cvss_vector
fields.description: The CVSS vector string, when a source gives one.

fields.name: si_remediation
fields.description: HOW to fix: the source's remediation text (Defender configuration RemediationOptions, Defender for Cloud remediationDescription) or SI's own report text. Unknown when no source says.

fields.name: si_remediation_type
fields.description: The kind of fix: patch | configuration | upgrade | policy | manual. From the source (a security update = patch, a configuration remediation = configuration) or the report text; unknown when no source says.

fields.name: si_fix_reference
fields.description: The fix the source names: the security update (KB) / update id of a vulnerability.

fields.name: si_fix_available
fields.description: A fix exists (the source names a security update or a remediation).

fields.name: si_fix_remediation
fields.description: HOW to fix this finding, shown with it: the source's fix (Defender configuration RemediationOptions, Defender for Cloud remediation, the security update of a vulnerability) or SI's own how-to-fix text for its reports. The Risk Analysis rows carry it as a column of the same name.

fields.name: si_fix_recommended_update
fields.description: The security update Defender vulnerability management recommends for a vulnerability (RecommendedSecurityUpdate, e.g. KB5040948); several are joined with a semicolon. Empty when Defender names none.

fields.name: si_fix_recommended_update_id
fields.description: The id of the recommended security update (RecommendedSecurityUpdateId, e.g. 5040948); several are joined with a semicolon.

fields.name: si_affected_software
fields.description: The affected software of a vulnerability as Name Version (Vendor), from Defender vulnerability management; several are joined with a semicolon.

fields.name: si_epss
fields.description: The EPSS score of the CVE: the probability (0 to 1) that it is exploited in the next 30 days (Defender vulnerability management EpssScore). Sortable; empty when Defender gives none.

fields.name: si_cve_supportability
fields.description: Whether Defender vulnerability management supports the CVE (CveSupportability: Supported, Not Supported, SupportedInPremium).

fields.name: si_cve_tags
fields.description: How Defender tags the CVE on the device (CveTags, e.g. ZeroDay, NoSecurityUpdate); several are joined with a semicolon.

fields.name: si_exploited_cves
fields.description: The CVE ids of a vulnerability summary row that have a known exploit (the same exploit flag as the finding's HasExploit); empty when none.

fields.name: si_exploited_cve_count
fields.description: How many CVE ids of a vulnerability summary row have a known exploit (0 when none).

fields.name: si_cve_mitigation_status
fields.description: Whether a workaround or mitigation is in place for the CVE on the device (Defender vulnerability management CveMitigationStatus).

fields.name: si_eos_status
fields.description: The end-of-support state of the affected software (Defender vulnerability management EndOfSupportStatus: EOS Version, Upcoming EOS Version, EOS Software, Upcoming EOS Software).

fields.name: si_eos_date
fields.description: When support for the affected software ends or ended (EndOfSupportDate).

fields.name: si_affected_path
fields.description: Where on the device the affected software was found: a few disk and registry paths (Defender vulnerability management software evidence), joined with a semicolon.

fields.name: si_evidence
fields.description: What the source found that makes this a finding: the offending value of a configuration (Defender Context), the certificate or the extension concerned.

fields.name: si_exploit_types
fields.description: The kinds of exploit known for the CVE (Defender vulnerability API exploitTypes, e.g. Remote, Local, PrivilegeEscalation); joined with a semicolon.

fields.name: si_exposed_devices
fields.description: How many devices in the tenant are exposed to the CVE (Defender vulnerability API exposedMachines).

fields.name: si_exposure_impact
fields.description: How much the tenant's exposure score falls when the Defender security recommendation behind the finding is carried out (Defender recommendations API exposureImpact). A configuration finding takes its own recommendation; a vulnerability takes the recommendation of its affected software (the highest when it concerns several). Context only -- it changes no risk factor and no score. Empty when Defender gives none or the permission is not granted.

fields.name: si_active_alert
fields.description: An active alert is associated with the Defender security recommendation behind the finding (Defender recommendations API activeAlert; for a vulnerability, the recommendation of its affected software). Context only -- it changes no risk factor and no score. Empty when Defender does not say or the permission is not granted.

fields.name: si_source_first_detected
fields.description: When the SOURCE first reported the finding (Defender for Cloud firstEvaluationDate). si_first_detected stays SecurityInsight's own first detection.

fields.name: si_source_first_seen
fields.description: When the SOURCE first saw this finding on this asset (the protection score's age): Defender for Endpoint firstSeenTimestamp of the device-CVE pair (the software vulnerabilities export), Defender for Cloud firstEvaluationDate, the first Shodan banner of a public IP. Empty where the source gives no such date (secure configurations, identity and exposure posture checks). si_first_detected stays SecurityInsight's own first detection.

fields.name: si_fix_owner
fields.description: Who is assigned to fix the finding in its source (Defender for Cloud governance assignment owner). Comes with Defender CSPM; says "no data (licence missing or not collected yet)" when the tenant shows no sign of it.

fields.name: si_fix_due_date
fields.description: When the fix is due in its source (Defender for Cloud governance remediation due date).

fields.name: si_fix_grace_period
fields.description: Whether the governance assignment has a grace period (Yes / No): during it the recommendation does not lower the secure score.

fields.name: si_secure_score_control
fields.description: The Defender for Cloud secure score control the recommendation counts in.

fields.name: si_secure_score_gain
fields.description: The points that secure score control can still gain in the subscription (its maximum minus its current score) -- what fixing its recommendations is worth.

fields.name: si_attack_path_count
fields.description: How many Defender for Cloud attack paths the recommendation is part of.

fields.name: si_attack_paths
fields.description: The names of those attack paths. Comes with Defender CSPM; says "no data (licence missing or not collected yet)" when the tenant shows no sign of it.

fields.name: si_policy_definition_id
fields.description: The Azure Policy definition behind the recommendation (Defender for Cloud metadata policyDefinitionId).

fields.name: si_status_cause
fields.description: The source's own reason for the finding's status (Defender for Cloud status cause and description).

fields.name: si_image_digest
fields.description: The digest of the container image a finding is about.

fields.name: si_image_repository
fields.description: The repository of the container image a finding is about.

fields.name: si_certificate_expiry
fields.description: When the certificate of a certificate finding expires (Defender vulnerability management certificate inventory).

fields.name: si_certificate_thumbprint
fields.description: The thumbprint of the certificate of a certificate finding.

fields.name: si_remediation_effort
fields.description: The effort to fix, as the source rates it (Defender for Cloud implementationEffort: Low | Moderate | High).

fields.name: si_user_impact
fields.description: The impact of the fix on users, as the source rates it (Defender for Cloud userImpact: Low | Moderate | High).

fields.name: si_compliance_tags
fields.description: Compliance / benchmark references (CIS, NIST, ISO ...): Defender configuration Tags and benchmarks, Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance, or the report's data (finding-texts).

fields.name: si_mitre_tactics
fields.description: MITRE ATT&CK tactics (TA####): the source's own (Defender configuration RelatedMitreTactics, Defender for Cloud tactics) or the report's data.

fields.name: si_mitre_techniques
fields.description: MITRE ATT&CK techniques (T####): the source's own or the report's data.

fields.name: si_reference_url
fields.description: The reference for the finding (NVD for a CVE, the source's reference URL).

fields.name: si_portal_link
fields.description: Where to see the finding in its source's portal (Defender for Cloud azurePortal link, Entra / Defender portal link).

fields.name: si_published
fields.description: When the vulnerability was published (Defender vulnerability management PublishedDate).

fields.name: si_due_date
fields.description: When the finding is due: the ticket's due date (ServiceNow) or the SLA SI derives; unknown otherwise.

fields.name: si_asset_criticality
fields.description: The criticality of the asset the finding is on (from the CI: tier, CMDB criticality), as one word -- copied onto the finding so a report and the hand-off carry it.

fields.name: si_exemption
fields.description: The exemption that covered the finding at run time: { id, scope, state, expires, reason } (si_exemption_id keeps the id).

fields.name: si_ticket_state
fields.description: The state of the finding's ticket in the customer's ITSM (ServiceNow vulnerable item state), as read back.

fields.name: si_vuln_count
fields.description: How many vulnerabilities (distinct CVEs) Defender reports on the device. Empty when Defender has not assessed the device -- never read as none.

fields.name: si_vuln_critical_count
fields.description: How many of the device's vulnerabilities are Critical.

fields.name: si_vuln_high_count
fields.description: How many of the device's vulnerabilities are High.

fields.name: si_vuln_medium_count
fields.description: How many of the device's vulnerabilities are Medium.

fields.name: si_vuln_low_count
fields.description: How many of the device's vulnerabilities are Low.

fields.name: si_vuln_exploitable_count
fields.description: How many of the device's vulnerabilities have a known exploit.

fields.name: si_vuln_highest_cvss
fields.description: The highest CVSS score among the device's vulnerabilities.

fields.name: si_vulnerable_software_count
fields.description: How many software products on the device have at least one vulnerability.

fields.name: si_software_count
fields.description: How many software products Defender's software inventory lists on the device.

fields.name: si_software_eos_count
fields.description: How many software products on the device are past their end of support (Defender software inventory).

fields.name: si_software_eos
fields.description: The software products on the device past (or near) their end of support, as "vendor/product version (status, date)".

fields.name: si_vuln_newest_published
fields.description: The publication date of the newest vulnerability on the device.

fields.name: si_vuln_oldest_published
fields.description: The publication date of the oldest vulnerability still on the device.

fields.name: si_vuln_top
fields.description: The device's most severe vulnerabilities, each as its id and name side by side: "CVE id -- software (severity, CVSS, exploit available)". The findings themselves are in Risk Analysis.

fields.name: si_vuln_summary_status
fields.description: Why the device has no vulnerability summary when the whole tenant has no vulnerability data: "no data (licence missing or not collected yet)".

fields.name: si_config_assessed_count
fields.description: How many security settings Defender assessed on the device.

fields.name: si_config_noncompliant_count
fields.description: How many assessed security settings the device does not meet.

fields.name: si_config_highest_impact
fields.description: The highest impact among the security settings the device does not meet (Defender's own scale).

fields.name: si_config_assessed_at
fields.description: When Defender last assessed the device's security settings.

fields.name: si_config_noncompliant_categories
fields.description: The categories of the security settings the device does not meet (for example Antivirus, Operating system, Network).

fields.name: si_config_top
fields.description: The security settings the device does not meet with the highest impact, each as its id and name side by side: "configuration id -- name (category, impact)".

fields.name: si_config_summary_status
fields.description: Why the device has no security-setting summary when the whole tenant has no security-setting data: "no data (licence missing or not collected yet)".

fields.name: si_mdc_assessed_count
fields.description: How many Defender for Cloud assessments the resource has.

fields.name: si_mdc_unhealthy_count
fields.description: How many Defender for Cloud assessments of the resource are unhealthy. Empty when Defender for Cloud has no assessment of the resource -- never read as healthy.

fields.name: si_mdc_high_count
fields.description: How many of the resource's unhealthy assessments are High severity.

fields.name: si_mdc_medium_count
fields.description: How many of the resource's unhealthy assessments are Medium severity.

fields.name: si_mdc_low_count
fields.description: How many of the resource's unhealthy assessments are Low severity.

fields.name: si_mdc_oldest_unhealthy
fields.description: When the oldest of the resource's unhealthy assessments was first evaluated.

fields.name: si_mdc_newest_change
fields.description: When an unhealthy assessment of the resource last changed its status.

fields.name: si_mdc_top
fields.description: The resource's most severe unhealthy Defender for Cloud assessments, each as its id and name side by side: "assessment id -- name (severity)". The findings themselves are in Risk Analysis.
